exposure: age at cancer diagnosis (<14 years old, ≥14 years old)
cohort: Women born between 1973 and 1977 diagnosed with cancer in childhood or adolescence (age <21) and an age-matched comparison group from the general population
finding: Childhood and adolescent cancer survivors had an increased risk of various pregnancy and childbirth complications, including preeclampsia, labor dystocia, and emergency cesarean section, compared to an age-matched comparison group.
mod_finding: Childhood and adolescent cancer survivors were more likely to undergo induction of labor and have deliveries ending with vacuum extraction and emergency cesarean section.
